source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables

summary: sR is a statistical corrector component that captures correlations between register values and branch directions. It generates a 12-bit digest from the values of recently written logical registers using a Tomasulo-like tracking table. For each of 8 register banks, it evaluates available registers and selects the single most useful one using a usefulness weight table (UT). The selected digest is then hashed with the PC to index prediction weight tables (WT), contributing a scaled sum to the final statistical corrector output.

state.name: sR_WT
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (WT0, WT1, WT2)
state.indexing: PC + register digest hashed to h0, h1, h2

state.name: sR_UT
state.organization: 8 banks, 3 tables per bank (UT0, UT1, UT2)
state.entry_format: Vector of signed weights (wt_bits), one per logical register

state.name: sR_RegTable
state.entry_format: valid (1 bit), payload (max(rob_idx_bits, 12) bits), decay_ctr (decay_ctr_bits bits)

state.name: sR_InFlightState
state.organization: FIFO queue, one entry per in-flight branch
state.entry_format: Bitmask of valid registers at prediction time

algorithms.name: allocate_register
algorithms.notes: Decay counter is decremented globally on every decode to eventually invalidate stale digests.

algorithms.name: write_register_digest
algorithms.notes: Calculates the digest based on the register type and writes it to the payload. Only updates if the ROB index matches.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.pseudocode:
for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
  sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] = sR_RegTable[r].valid

sR = 0
for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  u_idx0 = hash_ut(PC, 0) % ut0_entries
  u_idx1 = hash_ut(PC, 1) % ut1_entries
  u_idx2 = hash_ut(PC, 2) % ut2_entries
  
  max_u = -99999
  best_reg = -1
  
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_RegTable[r].valid == 1:
      u_sum = sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][r] + sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][r] + sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][r]
      if u_sum > max_u:
        max_u = u_sum
        best_reg = r
        
  bank_sum = 0
  if best_reg != -1:
    digest = sR_RegTable[best_reg].payload
    w_idx0 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    w_idx1 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    w_idx2 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    bank_sum = sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] + sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] + sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2]
  
  if max_u > 0:
    sR = sR + int(bank_sum * useful_multiplier)
    
return sR
algorithms.notes: Selects the most useful valid register per bank to look up the weight tables.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.pseudocode:
for b in 0 .. num_banks - 1:
  available_regs = []
  for r in 0 .. num_logical_regs - 1:
    if (r % num_banks) == b and sR_InFlightState[branch.rob_index][r] == 1:
      available_regs.append(r)
      
  if length(available_regs) > 0:
    chosen_reg = available_regs[random_int() % length(available_regs)]
    
    u_idx0 = hash_ut(PC, 0) % ut0_entries
    u_idx1 = hash_ut(PC, 1) % ut1_entries
    u_idx2 = hash_ut(PC, 2) % ut2_entries
    
    u_delta = calculate_utility_delta(branch)
    sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[0][b][u_idx0][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[1][b][u_idx1][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] = saturate(sR_UT[2][b][u_idx2][chosen_reg] + u_delta, wt_bits)
    
    digest = sR_RegTable[chosen_reg].payload
    w_idx0 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 0) % wt0_entries
    w_idx1 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 1) % wt1_entries
    w_idx2 = hash_wt(PC, digest, 2) % wt2_entries
    
    w_delta = 1 if branch.direction == 1 else -1
    sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] = saturate(sR_WT[0][b][w_idx0] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] = saturate(sR_WT[1][b][w_idx1] + w_delta, wt_bits)
    sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] = saturate(sR_WT[2][b][w_idx2] + w_delta, wt_bits)
algorithms.notes: Randomly selects one register from those available at prediction time to update its usefulness and weight.

algorithms.name: recovery
algorithms.notes: Without a full Tomasulo RAT snapshot, recovery conservatively clears pending writes matching squashed ROBs. Completed wrong-path digests (valid=1) are left to decay naturally.

host_interfaces.description: The exact 64-bit value produced by the instruction to compute the digest.
host_interfaces.fallback: Supply zero as the digest or do not update the register table for this instruction.

host_interfaces.need: instruction destination logical register ID and ROB index at decode
host_interfaces.description: To track which in-flight instruction will write each logical register.
host_interfaces.fallback: Omit tracking for instructions missing this information.

host_interfaces.description: To determine the correct digest generation method.

host_interfaces.need: notification of pipeline squash with squashed ROB indices
host_interfaces.description: To invalidate pending register writes from squashed instructions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Allow pending writes to complete and briefly pollute the digest table until they decay.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: sR_WT: 43008 bits, sR_UT: 9360 bits, sR_RegTable: 1495 bits, sR_InFlightState: 16640 bits
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Table 3 of the paper claims 53863 bits for sR. My total is 64503 bits. I am over by 10640 bits. The paper's total exactly covers WT, UT, and RegTable (43008 + 9360 + 1495 = 53863). It omits the 16640 bits needed for sR_InFlightState to snapshot the 65 valid bits per in-flight branch, which the update algorithm requires to know which registers were available at prediction time. Naming the host as the provider does not remove this from the budget at iso-storage.

parameters.name: num_logical_regs
parameters.storage_impact: Scales UT, RegTable, and InFlightState linearly

parameters.name: wt_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Scales WT and UT size linearly

parameters.name: rob_idx_bits
parameters.storage_impact: Determines payload size in RegTable if greater than 12

unit_tests.name: decay_counter_walks_down
unit_tests.given: An instruction completes and writes a register via write_register_digest, setting sR_RegTable decay_ctr to 255. Then 255 subsequent instructions are decoded via allocate_register.
unit_tests.expect: decay_ctr reaches 0, and the register's valid bit in sR_RegTable is cleared to 0.

unit_tests.name: int_digest_generation
unit_tests.given: An INT instruction completes with value 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF0 via write_register_digest.
unit_tests.expect: sR_RegTable payload receives the XOR-folded digest computed using count_leading_zeros (0) and count_trailing_zeros (4), with valid set to 1.

unit_tests.name: predict_selects_most_useful
unit_tests.given: sR_RegTable has valid digests for registers 0 and 8 (both in bank 0). sR_UT has a higher summed usefulness weight for register 8 than register 0.
unit_tests.expect: predict evaluates bank 0 using the digest of register 8 to index sR_WT, ignoring register 0.

unit_tests.name: update_random_selection
unit_tests.given: A branch commits via update, and its sR_InFlightState shows multiple registers were valid in bank 0 at prediction time.
unit_tests.expect: Only one randomly chosen register from bank 0 has its corresponding sR_UT and sR_WT entries modified.

unit_tests.name: recovery_clears_pending
unit_tests.given: An instruction allocates register 5, leaving it valid=0 and payload=ROB_ID. Then a pipeline squash occurs via recovery with that ROB_ID.
unit_tests.expect: sR_RegTable register 5 retains valid=0 but has its payload cleared to 0.

open_questions: U2: The figure does not label the wire that selects x0 vs x2.5 for the bank multiplier. Assumed it is driven by the bank's own max_u > 0 check.
U3: Count encoding for INT registers is ambiguous. Assumed it counts bits matching the sign bit, saturating at 63.
U4: FP register format classification and placement is ambiguous. Assumed bits are right-aligned at digest bit 3 as drawn.

The paper does not state the exact Tomasulo RAT recovery mechanism for sR_RegTable on a pipeline squash. Assumed a lightweight policy that leaves valid wrong-path digests to naturally decay, while clearing pending (valid=0) entries matching squashed ROBs.
The exact utility delta calculation for sR_UT during update is unstated. Assumed a standard usefulness update based on whether the bank's prediction alone matched the overall branch outcome.
